title: reachability-replaces-the-allowlist
intention: Make the build inspector's fire-path separation a REACHABILITY property — no tree machinery is transitively reachable from inspector.py — instead of a hand-maintained roster of innocent modules that a human has to widen, with a dated comment, every time something harmless gets composed.
why: THE ALLOWLIST'S SIX ENTRIES HAVE ONE WHY BETWEEN THEM, and that is arithmetic over the file rather than a preference: cairn.machines.chart.verdict (2026-07-29), re + cairn.machines.skill_block (2026-08-01), cairn.tools.import_sieve (2026-08-06), and cairn.tools.base.nest (2026-08-07, never admitted). Every dated comment says the same thing in different words — this module is tree-free. A list whose every element carries the same justification is a property somebody typed out longhand (Law 1: re-deriving a settled answer is a defect, six times). THE LIVED SYMPTOM is the standing red, and it is not 'the list is wrong': cairn.tools.base.nest entered the fire path in 047d633, nobody widened the list, and the corpus reported 88/87/1 that day with the ONE red named as something else entirely. A list maintained by memory goes stale silently and the tooth then reports a decision nobody made — the trouble's own words, 'an UNMADE DECISION wearing a passing sweep'. Law 4: a rule that matters is enforced by physics; an allowlist enforces nothing about the capability, only about whether a human remembered. Under a reachability rule cairn.tools.base.nest needs no signature at all — it reaches only __future__ and typing.
traces_to: Law 4 (physics, not policy) first; Law 1 (the settled answer re-derived six times) second; Law 8 (a tooth that reds for bookkeeping teaches its reader to widen the list) third.

falsifier.proves_green: PROOF GATE — cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py for the new rule kind, under that component's own stated convention, which is stricter than the class default and is adopted verbatim: 'Every catching tooth is PAIRED: the same rule shaken over a planted graph (must catch) and over the real corpus (must not), because either half alone is satisfied by a sieve made of solid sheet metal.' Plus cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector_nexus.py for the rule's first tenant, where the replaced tooth lives. Both sealed under the tester (netns). ENTRY GATE — BUILDME rides the chart (a berthed validate packet claiming this ticket) plus intent_berth and sorted_berth. EXIT GATE — PROVED refuses without a complete passing verdict artifact against this falsifier. EMISSION GATE — WATCHME is carried, so the probe must be armed at its berth before the crossing. CLEARANCE — the PROVED crossing reads owning_intention -> gated_by.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a tree module IS transitively reachable from inspector.py and the tooth passes — a closure that stops short; (2) the tooth reds on a module NOT actually reachable — a closure that over-reaches; (3) a clean result over a graph too small to have been read — HollowScan must survive the new kind rather than being a property of the two old ones; (4) the allowlist tuple or the hand-written transitive half is still standing anywhere after this lands — replacing means removing, or the corpus carries two rules for one constraint; (5) the denied set ends up stated in the PROOF rather than at build_inspector's own address, which re-creates the list-in-a-proof defect one hop out and contradicts import_sieve's charter on rule ownership; (6) the per-module dynamic-import check is dissolved along with the allowlist. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: if the denied set has to GROW to keep the tooth honest, then naming the capability was not more general than naming the innocent and this node's whole claim is refuted.
falsifier.horizon: clauses (1)-(6) at PROVEME, both directions, planted-edge-must-catch and real-corpus-must-not — the paired shape import_sieve's own gate already demands. The wrong-shape signal is NOT answerable at prove: it needs corpus time, which is what the WATCHME carries.

children: none, because the node is one seam with two addresses and neither half is separately provable: the rule kind has no meaning without a declared rule to shake, and the declared rule has nothing to shake it with. Splitting them produces a child that cannot answer its own falsifier.
how: A third rule kind in cairn/tools/import_sieve/sieve.py — `unreachable`: the module at `from` may not TRANSITIVELY reach `modules` — built on the primitives already there (import_graph for the edges, _matches for the dotted-prefix question, module_name inverted into a name->path index so a dotted import resolves back to a file and the walk continues). Breadth-first from the entry module, returning the whole PATH that reached rather than the bare fact, so one run carries the complete diagnostic. HollowScan survives: a closure over a graph too small to have read the tree is 'did not run', never 'clean'. The RULE ITSELF — which capabilities the verdict path may not reach — is declared at build_inspector's own address, because import_sieve's charter says so in as many words ('Each RULE is owned by the component whose constraint it is ... and lives at that component's address, not here'). Then the proof's allowlist tuple AND the hand-written transitive half below its loop both go: replacing means removing, or the corpus carries two rules for one constraint. The per-module dynamic-import check does NOT go — it covers the hole the AST cannot see and is orthogonal to which direction the AST question is asked in.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-denied-set-does-not-grow) -> [PROVED] (closed 2026-08-12; the WATCHME is ARMED and standing — the node is proved, its efficacy claim is not, and that is the split the free summons exists for)

watchme.trigger: Every build inspection — the event that already fires. inspect() shakes the nest over a component and the reachability sieve is one of its meshes, so the closure is computed there anyway; the probe reads the result of that shake rather than re-walking the graph. No clock, no sweep, no second parse of the tree.
watchme.enough: The claim is 'naming the denied capability stops the list growing while naming the innocent did not.' The denominator is what the OLD rule would have cost: under the allowlist, every module newly reachable from inspector.py cost one human widening with a dated comment — six in six weeks, measured. ENOUGH = ten distinct modules have entered inspector.py's transitive closure since this landed while the denied set is unchanged (ten widenings not paid). KILLED IMMEDIATELY, one occurrence sufficing, if the denied set GAINS an entry to keep the tooth honest — the wrong-shape signal firing, which refutes the node rather than dinging it. A closure that never grows at all is NOT a pass: the instrument had no chance to discriminate, and the probe reports that as insufficient rather than as evidence.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact written against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the closure as measured (its size and the modules in it), the denied set as declared with its size, and the delta of both against the values recorded at this ticket's PROVED crossing — so the reader sees the two numbers the claim is a relation between, not one number and an assertion.
watchme.nexus: the build inspector's own sieve corpus — the same place the reach bands and the sole_path findings land, because a rule's efficacy is a finding about a rule and belongs where the other findings about rules are.
watchme.consumer: build_inspector, the owner of the fire-path constraint and the only component that can act on a finding that its own separation rule has started drifting. Law 6: the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act, never the probe's.

chart_claim: validate-20260812T163435-a01590933d1b — chart chain complete with real content; verdict berthed at verdict-20260812T170623-9e99fc374805
dissolves_trouble: the-inspectors-allowlist-tooth-is-red-on-an-import-it-never-admitted — LIVE, and its disposition_owed names only two options (widen the allowlist with a dated comment / drop the import). Akien was offered both and answered by ruling this built instead: 'i want the reachability rule to be built as part of a batch of things that get sailed after i tire of answering rulings and questions.' So the trouble is not being fixed, it is being made unable to recur.
filed_edges: (a) A DOTTED NAME THAT RESOLVES TO NO FILE IS A DEAD END OF THE WALK. Safe today only because every denied capability is an IN-TREE module (cairn.machines.chart.tree, cairn.devices.librarian, cairn.devices.db_domain). The day a denied capability is a third-party dial, this walk stops short and says nothing. Named at cast rather than discovered at the crossing.

(b) THE SUBPROCESS AND THE DYNAMIC IMPORT STAY INVISIBLE — import_sieve's own edge (a), inherited whole. Reachability is strictly better at the question it asks and no better at the question it cannot ask, which is why the per-module dynamic-capability check survives as falsifier clause (6) rather than being folded in.

(c) NEXUS.PY STAYS ON THE HAND-WRITTEN ALLOWLIST, by decision at cast. Its allowlist is ('__future__', 'cairn.machines.chart.tree') — it ADMITS a tree door, by design, because the nexus is the graft's one legitimate cairn door. A reachability rule aimed at it would be aimed at nothing, and the tidy instinct that says 'convert both, they are in the same dict' is the drift this bound stops.

(d) THE DECLARATION SURFACE IS UNSETTLED AT CAST and is the survey stage's to settle: build_inspector has no existing declared-RULE surface — its sole_path rule is a dict literal in inspector.py at line 1638. Whether the denied set joins it there, becomes a charter field, or gets its own file is a build decision against what is actually there.

closed_by:
THE FALSIFIER RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what this component's own gate demands and is stricter than the class default. FORWARD: 28 teeth in cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py, green twice bare; the live corpus caught == [] for all three denied doors read separately; corpus 100 proofs / 100 green / 0 red, twice. BACKWARD, and this is the half that carries the weight: with sieve.reaches stubbed to return {}, FIVE teeth fail — including test_unreachable_catches_a_breach_two_hops_down and the real-corpus tooth, whose non-vacuity assert (closure > 5) refuses to go green over an empty walk — while 23 unrelated teeth stay green. And with `import cairn.devices.librarian` planted at cairn/tools/base/address.py, two hops out, the inspector's tooth reds with the whole route (cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector -> cairn.machines.chart.orient -> cairn.tools.base.address); the twelve-name allowlist it replaced returns [] against that same breach. Strictly wider coverage, measured head to head, arrived at without anyone widening a list.

WHAT WAS BUILT. (1) sieve.reaches(graph, start) — BFS forward transitive closure keeping the shortest chain to each file, folding __init__ through module_name, dead-ending on an unresolvable dotted name, raising on a start it never read. (2) A third rule kind `unreachable` inside catches(), guarded by the HollowScan floor because size is checked BEFORE the kind is dispatched — falsifier clause (3) holds for the new kind, not merely for the two that predate it. (3) build_inspector._FIRE_PATH: the DENIED capability declared once at the inspector's own address (13 modules — the graph tree by both its names, 5432, the inference host, and nine network dialers), a fire_path_unreachable sieve, and the roster entry that makes it mesh #20. (4) The allowlist tuple and the five-module reach loop STRUCK from test_inspector_nexus.py; the proof now COMPOSES the declaration, including deriving TREE_DOORS from _FIRE_PATH['modules'] rather than restating it. (5) A probe at cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/does_the_denied_set_stay_put.py, first tenant of a new probes/.

THE TWO THINGS I WAS WRONG ABOUT, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. (a) I predicted _SOLE_PATH already covered the inference host so the fire-path rule need not name it. Planting `import cairn.devices.inference_domain.route` leaves _SOLE_PATH GREEN — inference_domain is precisely the component permitted to dial — while the verdict path gains the ability to ask an LLM. WHO MAY DIAL and WHAT THE VERDICT MAY REACH are different questions and the second is not implied by the first. (b) I predicted the new sieve would mirror sole_path_holds exactly, including its per-row attribution. It does not. Per-row attribution rebuilt a 243-file graph 24 times, added 22s to every inspection and timed out this component's own proof at 120s; re-read afterwards, the analogy was wrong on the merits too — sole_path's constraint binds EVERY component, this one binds ONE PATH, and that path is build_inspector's.

WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Closes the live trouble the-inspectors-allowlist-tooth-is-red-on-an-import-it-never-admitted: cairn.tools.base.nest stopped being an unmade decision without anyone having to decide it, which is the whole shape of the fix. Does NOT close the bet that the denied set stays put while the closure grows — that needs corpus time and left here as the WATCHME, not as a criterion. Left standing and named: reach_of bands stop at the module boundary, so the two tree-walking sieves band 0 and the nest runs its most expensive meshes first; the dynamic-import check still names 5 modules by hand while the closure holds 17; a subprocess dials and imports nothing (filed edge (b), unchanged).
